title: Native forms of `replace`, `reverse`, `ascii` and `repeat`; `replace` takes no pattern per row
verdict: exact with a literal pattern; a pattern per row is refused by Polars
description: Polars has no `ascii` or `repeat` and reverses grapheme clusters (polars-string-functions-missing, polars-reverse), but these expressions give the reference's values. `str.replace_all(p, r, literal=True)` with a literal `p` replaces every occurrence as Python's `str.replace` does: the empty pattern matches at every character boundary (`-a-b-c-`), and `r` is taken literally (`\1` stays). `str.split("")` splits into code points (`split_chars`), so `list.reverse` and `list.join("")` reverse by code point. `str.slice(0, 1).str.encode("hex").str.to_integer(base=16)` is the first character's UTF-8 bytes as an integer, NULL for `''`, which decodes exactly to its code point. `repeat_by(n).list.join("")` is `s` repeated `n` times, `''` for `n` = 0, but `''` (not NULL) for a NULL `s`. A pattern per row is refused: `replace_all` with a column pattern raises `ComputeError: dynamic pattern length in 'str.replace' expressions is not supported yet` (a six-row frame once did not raise; 20,000 rows did, on both engines).
reference: `Text.replace` is `str.replace`, `Text.reverse` reverses the code points, `Text.ascii` is the first code point (0 for `''`), `Text.repeatStr` repeats `n` times (`''` for `n` ≤ 0); NULL in, NULL out.

provenance.notes: Each test compares the expression with the Python it replaced on 4,000 strings of a, b, é, 日, e+U+0301, a flag's two regional indicators, %, _, backslash, ., (, space, newline, A and É, with NULLs, on the streaming engine. The same checks on 20,000 rows ran on both engines with no mismatch. Polars 2.1.0 (Python), macOS arm64.

evidence.note: replace_all: a scalar pattern and value take replace_literal_all; a scalar pattern with a value per row, an escaped regex with NoExpand; a pattern per row bails out
an empty separator splits into characters (`split_chars`)
hex_encode: the string's UTF-8 bytes as hex
